handbookNote: Connecticut Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-02 R26 population-tier broker buildout. Exam vendor: PSI, under contract with the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection (DCP). Exam mechanics: 80 national + 40 state = 120 items, 75% to pass (a separate scored threshold per portion), confirmed via DCP landscape research (which independently reported the exact 80-national/40-state/75%-pass structure, distinct from the Salesperson exam's 80-national/30-state/70%-pass structure). Duration (180 minutes: 120 min national + 60 min state) is DERIVED from Connecticut's own confirmed internal timing ratio rather than borrowed from another state: PSI's real, directly-fetched 2019 Connecticut Salesperson Candidate Information Bulletin (proctor2.psionline.com, found via the site's own existing ct_re_salesperson bulletin link) shows Connecticut consistently allocates 1.5 minutes per item on both its general portion (80 items/120 min) and its state portion (30 items/45 min) -- applying that same confirmed 1.5 min/item ratio to the Broker exam's 40-item state portion (vs. Salesperson's 30) yields 60 minutes, for 180 minutes combined. This is a same-state internal-consistency inference, not a Broker-specific bulletin citation (Connecticut's current PSI candidate portal for the Broker exam specifically is JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched directly), but is considerably better-grounded than an earlier draft of this note that borrowed Kentucky's unrelated 240-minute figure. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=120, exam_duration_sec=10800, pass_percent=75, min_correct=90. Broker eligibility: 3 years as an actively licensed CT salesperson (1,500 supervised hours, 4+ transactions) plus 90+ hours of broker-level coursework. NATIONAL PORTION (80 items) drafted against PSI's real 11-section outline structure (confirmed via Kentucky's and Oklahoma's official bulletins to be PSI's standard national framework, though per-state weights vary): Property Ownership, Land Use Controls and Regulations, Valuation and Market Analysis, Financing, General Principles of Agency, Property Condition and Disclosures, Contracts, Leasing and Property Management, Transfer of Title, Practice of Real Estate, Real Estate Calculations -- drafted from the start with all 11 sections (learned from the Kentucky/Oklahoma builds, where 2 sections were initially missed and needed a same-day gap-fill; this build avoided repeating that gap). Connecticut-specific item weights were not independently confirmable (same JS-portal blocker as duration) so KY's confirmed raw item counts were used as a reasonable per-section drafting guide rather than an assumed-exact match. CONNECTICUT STATE PORTION (40 items) sourced against Connecticut General Statutes Title 20, Chapter 392 (Real Estate Brokers and Salesmen) via the official Connecticut General Assembly site (cga.ct.gov), which reliably truncated mid-fetch past roughly Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-317 on every attempt across all 5 state-topic drafting agents -- sections beyond that point (§§ 20-321 through 20-325m and later) were confirmed only by citation/heading via the chapter's table of contents, with agents deliberately declining to draft any mechanical detail (fine amounts, day-counts, retention periods) for those sections rather than guess. Genuine gaps flagged and left undrafted rather than guessed: Connecticut's exact general CE-hour renewal requirement (only the 6-hour military-service-exemption figure in § 20-314(f) could be confirmed), the § 20-324k trust-account deposit-timing day-count, a possible Guaranty Fund per-licensee aggregate cap distinct from the $25,000 per-claim/per-transaction figure, the exact annual Guaranty Fund assessment fee, and full body text for §§ 20-321 through 20-325m. One cross-file inconsistency was caught and fixed during this build: an initial licensing-requirements question incorrectly asserted salesperson licenses share the broker's Nov 30/even-year expiration date; a sibling drafting agent's independently-verified statute text showed salesperson licenses run on a separate, offset cycle, so the question was corrected to describe only the broker cycle. This bank was drafted across 16 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national + 5 state-law categories: Licensing Requirements, License Status & Broker Offices, Guaranty Fund & Trust Accounts, Disciplinary Actions, Agency & Disclosures), each instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js, producing a final near-even 25.1/25.0/25.0/25.0% A/B/C/D distribution. 597 raw questions drafted against a 120-item exam -- a 4.98:1 pool ratio, essentially at the standing 5:1 target.
